ops.title: PR 1316: settle pending judges before a one-shot runner exits
ops.description: Owner: PR #1316 implementation lane (agentic-judge-landing). Static review only; no tests run. Evidence: desk-runner.py:1893-1901, :5567-5571, :8955-8956 and :9033-9035/:9056-9057; tests/test_desk_runner.py:961-972 and :984-989. Pending judgments live only on the new Runner. Both --once loops exit after the asking pass, and Landing.drain ignores the judge pool; even if the executor finishes during Python shutdown, no caller consumes the verdict. Repeated --once invocations recreate the same problem. The autouse synchronous judgment mock hides it in the alarm tests. Next executable step: implement explicit one-shot judgment draining and decision collection, or persist pending decisions for a later invocation; add CI coverage using the real asynchronous wrapper.

ops.text: A delayed yes/None/unsure in --once emits the required alarm or fresh-row record before completion, or is durably collected on the next invocation.
A delayed no in --once emits the required JUDGE-SILENCED or TAP-KEPT outcome exactly once.
